reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Treating grades as numbers and averaging them.
Moving the joint at different speeds between assessments.
Recording the grade without the muscle group and position.
name: Modified Ashworth Scale

version.label: Modified Ashworth Scale (Bohannon & Smith 1987)
version.detail: Six grades: 0, 1, 1+, 2, 3, 4. The original Ashworth scale (1964) has five grades without 1+ and is a different version.

purpose: Grades resistance to passive movement (muscle tone) at one joint.
intendedPopulation: Patients with spasticity from brain or spinal cord disorders.

calculatorNotice.title: Ordinal grade
calculatorNotice.message: 1+ lies between 1 and 2. Grades are categories, not measurements, so they should not be added or averaged.

inputDefinitions.label: Resistance to passive movement

options.label: Slight increase: catch and release, or minimal resistance at the end of the range
Slight increase: catch, then minimal resistance through less than half of the range
More marked increase through most of the range, but the part moves easily
Considerable increase; passive movement is difficult
Affected part rigid in flexion or extension

inputDefinitions.help: Move the joint through its full range over about one second.

inputDefinitions.label: Side
inputDefinitions.help: Added to the copied result; it does not change the grade.

resultStates.label: No increase in tone
resultStates.summary: No increase in muscle tone at this joint at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Tone varies with position, time of day and medication; other joints may differ.

resultStates.label: More marked increase
resultStates.summary: Increased tone through most of the range; the part still moves easily.

resultStates.label: Rigid
resultStates.summary: Affected part rigid in flexion or extension.
resultStates.detail: Assess passive range for fixed contracture; the Modified Tardieu Scale separates contracture from spasticity.

clinicalContext.text: Grades resistance to passive movement at one joint.
Widely used to document spasticity and response to treatment.

clinicalInsights.text: MAS does not distinguish spasticity from contracture or rigidity; the Modified Tardieu Scale tests at different speeds.
At grades 3–4, check passive range of motion for contracture.

limitations.text: Measures resistance, which mixes neural (spasticity) and non-neural (stiffness, contracture) components.

limitations: Reliability is moderate, especially in the lower limb and around grades 1 and 1+.

confounders.factor: Time of day and recent medication

whatItDoesNotTellYou: The neural versus contracture component of resistance.
Function or the effect of spasticity on daily life.

guideSections.what: A six-grade ordinal scale (0, 1, 1+, 2, 3, 4) of resistance to passive movement.
guideSections.whenToUse: Documenting spasticity and change after treatment (e.g. botulinum toxin, intrathecal baclofen, rehabilitation).
guideSections.howToPerform: Position the patient consistently (usually supine). Move the joint through its full range over about one second. Grade the resistance felt. Record muscle group, side and position.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Use with passive range of motion and functional assessment; MAS alone does not separate spasticity from contracture.

sources.citation: Bohannon RW, Smith MB. Interrater reliability of a modified Ashworth scale of muscle spasticity. Phys Ther. 1987;67(2):206-207.
